reason: Section 110 is a focused advisory-views validity rule before council makes by-laws under the Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Written advisory views before council makes a by-law

evidenceText: shall request in writing the written views

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections require written views on proposed by-laws or later changes, make request for views a validity condition, require majority support if views are not followed, and deem approval after 30 days or longer council-set time.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when council must request advisory views, how ignoring them affects voting, and when approval is deemed.

reason: Section 111 is a large public-notice source with separate topics for notice timing and methods, notice contents and objections, and amendments, validity timing, and rezoning notice exceptions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: By-law objection time, place, and public notice methods

evidenceText: fix a time and place for the consideration of objections

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require council to fix the time and place for objections, give newspaper or website notice with specified timing, state by-laws excluded from section 111, and allow social media posting.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how council fixes objections and gives public notice before making by-laws under the Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Notice contents, public inspection, written objections, and speaking rights

evidenceText: shall set forth a description of the area affected

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections prescribe the contents of the notice, require inspection availability, require council to hear and consider written objections, and allow persons to speak for or against written objections.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what public notices must contain and what inspection, objection, and speaking rights follow.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Substantial amendments, six-month validity limit, and rezoning notice exception

evidenceText: within six months after the day that the notice was given

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections repeat notice for substantial amendments, impose a six-month validity requirement for making and submitting by-laws, and excuse a second newspaper notice for certain rezonings if nearby owners are advised or a property notice is posted.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what happens after substantial amendment, the six-month validity condition, and when a second rezoning notice is unnecessary.

reason: Section 112 is a coherent Minister approval, filing, publication, application package, and invalidity-saving rule.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister approval, land registration filing, publication, and application package

evidenceText: apply to the Minister for approval

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections require approval application, filing, public notice and Minister copy, specify accompanying documents, and save approved plans or schemes from invalidity for content defects.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the approval, filing, notice, application materials, and content-defect effect for council planning documents.

reason: Section 113 is a focused enhanced-vote rule triggered by written objections to zoning amendments.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: One-third landowner objection and majority vote for zoning amendments

evidenceText: signed by the owners of at least one-third

proposedGroups.reason: The section states that certain zoning amendment by-laws are not valid unless a majority of council members vote in favour when objections are signed by owners of at least one-third of affected nearby land.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a zoning amendment needs majority support because of written objections by affected nearby landowners.

reason: Section 114 is a coherent construction freeze rule tied to proposed zoning, deferred widening, controlled access street, or rural-plan zoning provisions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Construction freeze after objection hearing is fixed

evidenceText: prohibit a development in the area affected

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections allow council to prohibit development in the affected area by resolution and state that the resolution expires after 14 days unless notice is published on time.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when council may impose a construction freeze for proposed land-use controls and when the freeze resolution stops being effective.

reason: Section 115 is a narrow Ministerial power to require review of a plan or development scheme.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister-required review of plans or development schemes

evidenceText: may require a council to review

proposedGroups.reason: The section allows the Minister to require council to review a plan or development scheme if the Minister considers review necessary.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that the Minister may require council to review a plan or development scheme when considered necessary.

reason: Section 116 is a narrow consultation permission allowing council to seek the Director's comments on a proposed by-law.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Director comments on proposed by-laws

evidenceText: may submit a proposed by-law to the Director

proposedGroups.reason: The section permits council to submit a proposed by-law to the Director for comments.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that council may ask the Director for comments on a proposed by-law.

reason: Section 117 is a coherent amendment and repeal rule for by-laws and adopted plans or development schemes.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Amending, repealing, revising, or replacing by-laws, plans, and schemes

evidenceText: may make a by-law that

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections authorize amending or repealing by-laws, plans, and schemes; apply existing provisions with modifications; and deem zoning by-law revisions or replacements to be amendments.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how council may amend or repeal planning by-laws, plans, and schemes, and when zoning revisions or replacements count as amendments.

reason: Section 118 states a focused no-injurious-affection rule for making, amending, or repealing by-laws or regulations.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: No injurious affection from by-law or regulation changes alone

evidenceText: shall not be deemed to be injuriously affected

proposedGroups.reason: The section states land is not deemed injuriously affected only because a by-law or regulation is made, amended, or repealed.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that making, amending, or repealing a by-law or regulation alone does not deem land injuriously affected.

reason: Section 119 states a focused severability rule for by-laws under the Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Severability of by-law provisions

evidenceText: The provisions of a by-law under this Act are severable

proposedGroups.reason: The section states that invalidity of one part of a by-law does not affect provisions that are not dependent or conditional on the invalid part.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how severability preserves independent by-law provisions when another part is invalid.

reason: Section 120 has distinct appeal topics: appeal grounds and the Board's hearing duty and filing deadlines.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Appeal grounds for development, permit, standards, action, subdivision, and instrument decisions

evidenceText: may appeal to the Board

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 120(1) lists appeal grounds for terms, prohibitions, refusals, approvals, permits, standards, council action, tentative or subdivision plans, instruments, and exemptions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the types of planning decisions and alleged errors or hardship that may be appealed to the Board.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Board hearing duty and appeal time limits

evidenceText: The time limit for making an appeal

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require the Board to hear appeals unless there are insufficient grounds and set 60-day or 10-day time limits depending on the appeal ground.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Board must hear an appeal and the applicable appeal deadlines.

reason: Section 121 is a large appeal-remedy source with separate topics for remedies by appeal type, referrals back, effective dates, invalid by-law provisions, and majority decisions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Board remedies for development, permit, standards, action, subdivision, and instrument appeals

evidenceText: the Board may

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections set the Board's powers to dismiss, order approvals or permits, revoke approvals or permits, vary or revoke terms, affirm or vary standards or action, and order plan, instrument, or exemption approvals.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what orders or remedies the Board may make for each class of appeal under section 120.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Referral back with directions and effective dates for Board decisions and orders

evidenceText: may refer a matter back

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections allow referral back with directions, permit the original decision-maker to affirm, revoke or vary, and state when Board decisions and immediate-compliance orders take effect.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Board may refer a matter back and when its decisions or immediate-compliance orders take effect.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Unauthorized by-law provisions and majority decisions of the Board

evidenceText: is not authorized by this Act

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections let the Board allow appeals or make orders when a by-law provision is unauthorized and the basis for the appealed action, and state that a majority decision is the Board's decision.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how unauthorized by-law provisions affect Board remedies and how Board decisions are made by majority.

reason: Section 122 is a focused publication duty for significant Board decisions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Annual publication of significant Board decisions

evidenceText: published annually

proposedGroups.reason: The section requires the Minister to cause publication of Board decisions the Minister considers significant.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who causes significant Board decisions to be published and how often.

reason: Section 123 is a coherent inspection and inquiry rule for matters pending before the Board.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Board-authorized inquiry, entry warrant, dwelling limit, and report evidence

evidenceText: may authorize a person to make an inquiry

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections allow the Board to authorize inquiry and inspection, permit entry warrant applications, restrict entry into private dwellings, and require reports to be available before hearing and received in evidence.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how Board-authorized inspections work, when warrants or dwelling consent are needed, and how inquiry reports are used.

reason: Section 124 separates general regulation-making subjects from regional land use plan regulation details and fee or Board-consultation rules.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: General regulations for public interest, regional plans, inclusionary zoning, fees, charges, easements, approvals, Board procedure, definitions, and administration

evidenceText: may make regulations

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 124(1) lists broad regulation-making subjects, including statements of public interest, regional plans, inclusionary zoning, fees, development charges, easements, approvals, Board procedure, definitions, and administration.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the main subjects on which the Lieutenant-Governor in Council may make general regulations under section 124.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regional land use plan regulation process, content, indicators, monitoring, regional differences, roles, and application

evidenceText: Without limiting paragraph (1)(b)

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 124(2) expands the regulation power respecting regional land use plans to process, notice, content, indicators, monitoring, different regional provisions, roles, and specific or general application.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the additional regulation topics specific to regional land use plans.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regional service commission fee crediting and Board consultation for appeal procedure regulations

evidenceText: shall consult with the Board

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections direct prescribed service fees to the regional service commission and require consultation with the Board before making appeal procedure regulations.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall where prescribed regional service commission fees are credited and when the Board must be consulted before regulations are made.
